title: Holistic health mediator and autoscale soft-handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a lightweight "health mediator" component that fuses multiple health signals (readiness, liveness, latency percentiles, queue length, memory pressure, KV-cache hit rate) into a continuous 'service fitness' score per region and storefront. The mediator will drive two behaviors: (1) emit a stable, decayed readiness signal to reduce flapping and autoscaler thrash; (2) coordinate a soft-handoff policy for cross-region failover and circuit-breaking that prioritizes preserving SLOs with graceful degradation rather than hard outages.

Why: Recent incidents show noisy probe signals and short-term spikes cause the autoscaler and regional failovers to oscillate, increasing error-budget burn and customer requests dropped during transient blips. We need a provably smoother control signal and an orchestration path for soft handoffs that preserves p95 latency and reduces error spikes.

Scope: Build mediator service, integrate it with runtime health probe exporters, a central fusion/decay function, autoscaler admission hook, and a failover controller that supports progressive traffic reweighting, synthetic warmups, and token-aware shedding. Deliverables: health mediator binary, integration tests, canary rollout, metrics/dashboards, runbook additions.

Design constraints and non-goals: Not rewriting underlying readiness probes; mediator consumes existing signals. Not changing model selection logic or user-facing API. It must be lightweight (<50ms evaluation), run colocated with control-plane agent, and operate with degraded inputs (e.g., partial telemetry).

Success metrics: reduce autoscaler thrash events by >=60% (thrash defined as scale-up followed by scale-down within 5 minutes), reduce transient 5xx spikes during regional failover by >=40%, keep p95 latency change <=+15% for impacted traffic during soft-handoff, and maintain error-budget burn rate improvement over 7 days.

Key technical approach: 
- Signal fusion: weighted exponential moving average per metric with configurable half-life. Default weights: readiness=0.4, p95 latency=0.25, queue_depth=0.15, mem_pressure=0.1, kv_hit=0.1. Weights are tunable via config per customer tier.
- Decay and hysteresis: exposable smoothing window and quorum gating so that sudden single-probe drops don't immediately mark region unfit.
- Confidence model: attach per-sample confidence score; low-confidence signals are downweighted.
- Soft-handoff orchestrator: when mediator signals cross thresholds, trigger progressive traffic reweighting across regions (5% steps with 30s dwell) combined with synthetic-warmup requests to prepare cold caches and KV caches.
- Autoscaler admission hook: mediator can tag requests or push admission flags to autoscaler to prevent immediate scaling actions for a grace period tied to the fitness trajectory.
- Circuit breaker integration: mediator emits graded breaker score, enabling token-aware shedding policies instead of full drop.

Rollout strategy: feature-flagged by account/region. Start canary in non-critical region (eu-west-2) with 5% traffic, observe for 48h, then expand to critical regions with staged ramp and SLO guard rails.

Risk and mitigations: risk of over-smoothing and delayed reaction -> keep local short-term emergency path (hard stop) for catastrophic resource exhaustion. Risk of configuration complexity -> provide sane defaults and monitored dashboards.

Links: design doc, runbook and draft dashboards are in links below.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Triage: scoped by Eng Reliability and SRE. Agreed to build mediator as control-plane adjunct, not a rewrite of probes.

2026-03-04 - Design review: PM and Runtime Eng gave feedback to add confidence scoring and allow per-customer weight overrides. Action: Marco to update design doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/holistic-health-mediator).
2026-03-05 - Prototype: initial fusion library implemented (rust) and unit tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/health-mediator/pull/21

2026-03-07 - Integration test: mediator running in staging with synthetic noise, found over-smoothing for spurts under 8s; adjusted half-life defaults and added 'safety spike detector' to bypass smoothing for severe degradation.
2026-03-09 - Blocker: infra quota for additional control-plane agents in eu-west-2. Ops ticket created: ENG-100441. Will delay canary by ~48h unless quota approved.
2026-03-10 - Next: implement autoscaler admission hook and add token-aware shedding proof-of-concept. Assigned to Marco.
acceptance_criteria: Mediator produces per-region continuous fitness score and exposes it as metric (health.mediator.fitness) with tags region, cluster, confidence.
Autoscaler admission hook honors mediator 'grace' flag and suppresses scale actions for configured window when fitness is improving.
Failover controller can perform progressive reweighting with synthetic warmups and completes a 50% traffic handoff without >15% p95 regression in target region.
Unit, integration and chaos tests added to CI; canary run for 48h in eu-west-2 with dashboards monitoring thrash, p95, error-budget burn.
Runbook updated and after-action checklist created for oncall during rollout.
rollout_plan: Canary: eu-west-2 non-critical accounts, 5% traffic, 48h observation
Stage 1: expand to 20% traffic and enable autoscaler admission hook, 72h observation
Stage 2: enable progressive soft-handoff and token-aware shedding, monitor 7d
Full: enable by default for all regions with opt-out flag for legacy customers
